text:
Maya: Heads up — we need to align on metric names/labels for the new routing/quotas dashboards. Runtime and infra teams must agree on OTel -> Prom mappings and cardinality limits.
Jason: +1. Do we have a proposed prefix/pattern?
Maya: Proposal draft: all metrics get `redwood_{area}_...` prefix. Examples: `redwood_api_requests_total`, `redwood_runtime_request_duration_seconds`, `redwood_gpu_utilization_percent`. Snake_case.
Rachel: Agree on prefix. Also need strict cardinality rules. Prom exploded labels are a real SRE pain.
Lina: For model labels, should we use `model_id` or `model_name`? We have human names and pinned versions.
Jason: Use `model_id` for stable identity (e.g., `m-gpt4o-001`), add optional `model_version` label if we need semantic release tags. Avoid free-text names.
Kyle: Product asks for `route` label (the API route) so we can disaggregate by feature. But routes include query params sometimes. We should normalize.
Dan: Agree — normalize `route` to path only (strip query and instance ids). We should also avoid `request_id`/`trace_id` in labels.
Maya: Cardinality policy proposal: max ~100 unique values per label for high-frequency metrics. For lower-frequency, maybe 500. Anything likely to be unbounded (user_id, session_id, request_id) must not be a label.
Rachel: Also propose a set of approved labels: `route`, `model_id`, `region`, `deployment`, `shard`, `priority_tier`, `quantization`, `error_type` (coarse), `team_owner`.
Lina: For model dimension, teams want rollups by family and by variant. Suggest adding `model_family` (e.g., gpt-4o) but keep it derived server-side to avoid cardinality.
Jason: Strongly recommend server-side label normalization and enforced enumerations for `priority_tier` and `quantization`.
Maya: Example Prom and OTel mapping for the runtime latency metric:```
# Prom
redwood_runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",model_id="m-gpt4o-001",region="us-west-2",deployment="dedicated-01"} 42
redwood_runtime_request_duration_seconds_count{...} 123
redwood_runtime_request_duration_seconds_sum{...} 12.3
# OTel attributes we accept: service.name=redwood-runtime, http.route=/v1/generate, redwood.model.id=m-gpt4o-001, cloud.region=us-west-2
```
Kyle: For the Console dashboards we plan: per-route request rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate by `error_type`, tokens_in/tokens_out, kv_cache_hit_ratio, average_batch_size, and GPU utilization.
Dan: Two practical items: (1) CI linting for new metrics (no high-cardinality labels, follow prefix), (2) a shared YAML schema repo for allowed labels and examples. I can add a check to the metrics linter.
Rachel: SRE will add a promql monitor that alerts if a label's cardinality spikes unexpectedly. infra-bot will post when cardinality crosses threshold.
infra-bot: INFO: new metric scanning enabled — will report label cardinality weekly.
Maya: Edge cases: private deployments need `customer_hash` for per-tenant dashboards. That's allowed but only for Private/Enterprise metrics and must be hashed and documented.
Lina: What about quantization/precision annotation? Might be useful for perf dashboards. `quantization` label values: `fp16`, `int8`, `q4_0`, etc. Keep small set.
Jason: One more: add `batch_size` as a gauge and `batch_size_bucket` histogram for batching analysis. Avoid including `batch_id` as label.
Maya: Action items: 1) I'll draft the canonical metrics labels doc and examples by EOD Friday. 2) Jason to add lint rule to runtime repo (check prefix + no blacklisted labels) — due next Wed. 3) Rachel to wire the new queries in Console staging and attach to per-route dashboards — due in two weeks. 4) Dan to add a YAML in `metrics-schema/` repo and CI lint — due next Tue.
Kyle: +1 to timeline. Product will provide a short list of required route breakdowns.
Lina: Can we also capture token-level metrics? tokens_in/tokens_out should be summed counters not labels.
Maya: Yes. Example metric list we agreed on (short): `redwood_api_requests_total`, `redwood_api_requests_errors_total`, `redwood_runtime_request_duration_seconds`, `redwood_tokens_in_total`, `redwood_tokens_out_total`, `redwood_runtime_batch_size_gauge`, `redwood_kv_cache_hits_total`, `redwood_gpu_utilization_percent`.
Jason: I'll open a PR with the runtime instrumentation changes and include example instrumentation snippet.
Maya: Thanks — would like a follow-up sync if any team hits a label whose cardinality is > threshold.
Rachel: We'll enable infra-bot alerts in staging first.
Kyle: LGTM :+1:
Lina: :tada:
Maya: Closing for now — feel free to ping me if you need clarifications.
